method: Convex hull, computed in the UTM plane, of the 1587 stations that sdMap.csv flags sd1500 = 1 and that the release marks as still operating (31 hull vertices), converted to latitude and longitude. Earlier version of this record used every station ever flagged (1640 rows, 32 vertices, 3158 km2); stations that have since stopped are now left out. Station positions are the northing and easting columns of sdMap.csv in the Pierre Auger Collaboration Open Data release 3 (20 March 2024, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10488964), which the Collaboration describes as "UTC" [sic] coordinates in metres (the data page does not state the zone or datum). They are read as UTM zone 19 south (central meridian 69 deg W) on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (EPSG:32719) because only zone 19 puts the numbers at Malargue (the converted stations span latitude 34.93 to 35.52 S and longitude 68.91 to 69.66 W), and WGS 84 is the GPS datum; this reading is this work's assumption, hence confidence approximate and accuracy_m 50. The hull is a computed outline, not a published boundary, and a convex hull slightly over-states a concave array.
name: Pierre Auger Observatory surface-detector array (1500 m spacing), convex hull of active stations
notes: Area of the hull 3098 km2 against the Collaboration's round "3000 km2" (+3.3%).

The Observatory paper (arXiv:1502.01323 section 1) says the array lies "between latitudes 35.0 and 35.3 S and between longitudes 69.0 and 69.4 W"; the converted stations span 34.93 to 35.52 S and 68.91 to 69.66 W, so that sentence is a rough statement, not the extent of the stations.
Licence: sdMap.csv is released under CC BY-SA 4.0; the derived geometry carries the attribution and the same licence name (share-alike).

summary.plain: The outline of the main Auger array of detector tanks, about 3100 square kilometres of Argentine plain, drawn from the Observatory's own published station positions.
